sections.h1: Revamp Your Smile: Understanding the Basics of Tooth Implants in McLean, VA
sections.h2: Understanding Tooth Implants: What Are They?
lead: 4 July 2024

Tooth implants, or dental implants, are a revolutionary solution for replacing missing teeth. These implants consist of titanium posts surgically inserted into the jawbone, acting as artificial tooth roots. Once the implants are securely in place, they provide a stable foundation for attaching prosthetic teeth, such as crowns, bridges, or dentures. This procedure not only restores the functionality of natural teeth but also enhances the appearance of your smile. Dental implants are designed to mimic the look and feel of natural teeth, providing a long-term solution that can last a lifetime with proper care.

sections.h1: Revolutionize Your Smile with Dental Implants in McLean, VA
lead: 4 August 2024

Dental implants are a revolutionary solution for replacing missing teeth, offering a permanent and natural-looking alternative to traditional dentures or bridges. A dental implant consists of a titanium post surgically placed into the jawbone, which acts as a replacement root for the missing tooth. This post provides a strong foundation for a crown, bridge, or denture, mimicking the appearance and function of natural teeth. The procedure not only restores the aesthetics of your smile but also enhances overall oral health by preventing bone loss and maintaining facial structure.

The importance of dental implants goes beyond cosmetic benefits. They are crucial in preserving jawbone health, which can deteriorate when teeth are lost. Unlike traditional bridges that require the alteration of adjacent teeth, dental implants do not compromise the integrity of surrounding natural teeth. They provide stability and prevent the shifting of teeth that can occur with missing teeth. Additionally, implants offer improved comfort and functionality compared to removable dentures, allowing for a more natural and confident eating and speaking experience. Dental implants are a superior choice for those looking to restore their smile and oral health.

The success of dental implants is rooted in their design and the biological process of osseointegration. During this process, the titanium implant post fuses with the jawbone, creating a strong and stable foundation for the artificial tooth. This integration ensures the implant functions like a natural tooth root, supporting and preventing bone resorption. The implant’s stability also contributes to the longevity and durability of the dental restoration, making it a reliable solution for tooth replacement.

The materials used in dental implants are chosen for their biocompatibility and strength. Titanium is the most commonly used material due to its ability to bond with bone tissue without causing adverse reactions. This metal is durable and lightweight, making it ideal for long-term use in the body. The crown or prosthetic tooth attached to the implant is typically made from porcelain or ceramic, which can be color-matched to blend seamlessly with natural teeth. Combining these high-quality materials ensures that dental implants look natural and withstand the forces of chewing and speaking, providing a lasting solution for missing teeth.

When considering dental implants, it is essential to choose the right specialist to ensure a successful outcome. While general dentists can perform implant procedures, a prosthodontist offers specialized training and expertise in restorative dentistry. Prosthodontists undergo additional years of education and training focused on restoring and replacing teeth, making them highly skilled in complex implant cases. They are also well-versed in managing complications and ensuring their patients’ best aesthetic and functional results.

sections.h1: Should I Upgrade My Smile From Traditional Dentures To All-on-4 Dental Implants In McLean, VA?
sections.h2: The Reasons Why You Should Upgrade Your Smile From Traditional Dentures To All-on-4 Dental Implants In McLean, VA
lead: 2 December 2023

Traditional dentures are commonly used when people have lost all or most of their teeth due to dental disease, injury, or age. A traditional denture has a flesh-colored acrylic base, which fits over the patient’s gums, and teeth, which are usually made of acrylic or porcelain material. When people no longer want, or no longer can, wear traditional dentures, then they should upgrade their smile to All-on-4 dental implants in McLean, VA.

Interested in learning more about why people should upgrade their smile from traditional dentures to All-on-4 dental implants? Continue reading to learn more about why people should upgrade their smile to All-on-4 dental implants.

All-on-4 dental implants offer a host of advantages over traditional dentures. Here are the specific reasons why people should upgrade their smile from traditional dentures to All-on-4 dental implants.

items.h3: Permanent Full Arch Tooth Replacement Option:
text: All-on-4 dental implants should replace traditional dentures because they are a permanent full arch tooth replacement option. Traditional dentures are made to just sit on the patient’s gums and do not become a permanent part of their smile. The prosthesis for All-on-4 implants, on the other hand, is fixed to the patient’s mouth with four dental implant posts.

When placed in the patient’s jawbone, the dental implant posts fuse with the jawbone in a process called osseointegration. After the dental implant posts have fully fused with the jawbone, they become a permanent part of the patient’s smile. Once the prosthesis is attached to the dental implants, patients will have a beautiful and long-lasting new smile.

items.h3: Give Patients A Beautiful New Smile:
text: In terms of aesthetic beauty, All-on-4 dental implants give patients a better-looking new smile than traditional dentures. This is because the color, shape, and size of the full arch prosthesis are custom-made to look natural and aesthetically enhance the patient’s smile. Traditional dentures, on the other hand, are bulky and will not give patients a natural and better-looking new smile.

Unlike traditional dentures, All-on-4 dental implants preserve the patient’s jawbone density. This is because the dental implant posts, in an All-on-4 dental implant procedure, stimulate the patient’s jawbone once they have been permanently placed in it. This stimulation regenerates jawbone density, giving patients a strong and healthy new smile that they can depend on to live their lives normally.

All-on-4 dental implants are a more cost-effective full arch tooth replacement option than traditional dentures. Although the upfront cost of traditional dentures might be lower than All-on-4 dental implants, the maintenance and replacement costs that come with traditional dentures can add up over time.
On the other hand, with proper care and regular dental check-ups, All-on-4 implants can last a lifetime, making them a worthwhile full arch tooth replacement option.

items.h3: Gives A New Smile In One Day:
text: For All-on-4 dental implant procedures, when the dental implant posts have been securely placed in the patient’s jawbone, the temporary prosthesis can be attached to them in the same surgical appointment. The temporary prosthesis is what allows patients to get a brand-new smile in one day. This is a stark contrast to traditional dentures, which may require several fittings and adjustments over a span of weeks or months.

For individuals who have experienced significant tooth loss, the decision to upgrade from traditional dentures to All-on-4 dental implants can be life-changing. Not only do All-on-4 dental implants offer superior comfort, functionality, and aesthetics to traditional dentures, they also contribute to better oral health and overall quality of life for the patient.

posts/uncovering-the-mystery-the-in-dept.title: The In-Depth Guide to Dental Implants | Dr. Nahlah
posts/uncovering-the-mystery-the-in-dept.description: An in-depth guide to dental implants: the types available, the procedure step by step, osseointegration and caring for implants afterwards.

sections.h1: Uncovering the Mystery: The In-depth Guide to Dental Implants
sections.h2: Types of Dental Implants in McLean, VA
lead: 14 October 2024

Dental implants are not merely another aesthetic restoration but a fantastic solution for lost or damaged teeth. They assist in bridging the gap, providing both function and form. The technology behind them relies on a simple but elegant scientific concept- osseointegration. This is the physiological process where the implant integrates with the jawbone. Implant materials, often titanium, fuse with the bone, forming a stable foundation for replacement teeth, mimicking the functionality and feel of natural teeth.

The most relevant to patients are endosteal and subperiosteal implants. Endosteal implants find their place in healthy jawbones, while subperiosteal implants rest above the jawbone beneath the gum tissue. Each presents unique advantages catering to different conditions and patients’ needs, though the best choice is always determined after a careful specialist examination.

Both options provide a durable, aesthetically pleasing outcome tailored to enhance the patient’s oral function and overall appearance. With advancements in dental technology, implants have become a highly successful and accessible treatment, restoring confidence and improving the quality of life for patients with missing teeth.

The dental implant procedure has multiple steps, from consultation to post-operative care. It begins with a thorough assessment, followed by implant placement and abutment connection. lead: 24 December 2023

By going to a skilled and trusted dental office, people can get their dental implants in McLean, VA expertly placed. Once the dental implants have been strategically and securely placed in the patient’s jawbone, however, they will need to take care of their new teeth. When dental implants are properly taken care of, they can last a long time.
Want to learn more about how to properly take care of dental implants? Continue reading to learn about how to best take care of dental implants so that they are long-lasting.
When dental implants are properly taken care of, they can give patients a long-lasting new smile. The following are the specific ways dental implants can be properly taken care of:

text: In order to properly take care of dental implants, they should be regularly brushed and flossed. Just like natural teeth, dental implants can accumulate plaque and tartar, which if left unchecked, can lead to gum disease and dental implant failure. Brushing twice a day with a soft-bristled toothbrush removes the daily accumulation of plaque and food debris, protecting both the patient’s dental implant and their surrounding gum tissue.

Flossing, on the other hand, reaches the areas that a toothbrush cannot, such as the spaces between the teeth and the gumline. Regular flossing helps prevent the build-up of bacteria and plaque in these areas, reducing the risk of infections that could compromise the health and longevity of the dental implants.

Regular dental check-ups and cleanings play a pivotal role in patients maintaining the health and longevity of their dental implants. During dental check-ups and cleanings, the patient’s teeth and dental implants will be thoroughly cleaned, removing any hard-to-reach plaque or tartar that could lead to gum disease. The condition of the patient’s dental implants will also be checked, ensuring that they are secure and functioning correctly.

Getting regular dental check-ups is also an opportunity to get any potential issues detected early. If any signs of dental infection or damage are noticed, they can be promptly taken care of so the dental implants can last a long time.

Avoiding damaging habits is integral to the longevity and health of patient’s dental implants. Habits such as chewing on hard items like ice or hard candy, or using teeth as tools to open packages, can lead to the crown of the dental implant chipping or fracturing. Smoking and excessive alcohol consumption can also compromise the healing process of dental implants and impair the long-term health of the gum and bone surrounding the dental implant.

The condition of the patient’s dental implants will also be checked, ensuring that they are secure and functioning correctly.

Getting regular dental check-ups is also an opportunity to get any potential issues detected early. If any signs of dental infection or damage are noticed, they can be promptly taken care of so the dental implants can last a long time.

Avoiding damaging habits is integral to the longevity and health of patient’s dental implants. Habits such as chewing on hard items like ice or hard candy, or using teeth as tools to open packages, can lead to the crown of the dental implant chipping or fracturing. Smoking and excessive alcohol consumption can also compromise the healing process of dental implants and impair the long-term health of the gum and bone surrounding the dental implant.

sections.h2: Why Consider Dental Implants? Protect Your Smile and Well-Being!
lead: 20 October 2024

Dental implants in McLean, VA are small titanium posts that are surgically placed in your jawbone underneath your gum line. They allow your dentist to mount replacement teeth onto them as they provide the same support and stability that a root would for your natural teeth.

Why should you consider dental implants, you ask? For starters, they can help prevent your facial structure from changing. When you lose a tooth, you also lose the root, which results in bone loss. Also, missing teeth can affect your ability to chew and speak properly. So, if you’re missing a tooth, consider your replacement options for the sake of your physical and mental well-being.
Dental implants are custom-made to match the shape and color of your original teeth, which makes the process seamless:
Your dentist will evaluate your oral health to determine if you’re a good candidate for the procedure.
The titanium post will be surgically placed into your jawbone, followed by a healing period where the bone will grow around the implant to hold it in place.
An abutment will be attached to the implant, and finally, a replacement tooth designed to match your natural teeth will be mounted onto the abutment.

Choosing dental implants provides numerous advantages over other tooth replacement solutions. They have the appearance and feel of your natural teeth, and unlike dentures, they don’t slip or shift in your mouth, providing a robust and stable foundation for your artificial teeth. Plus, they have an impressive lifespan, often lasting a lifetime with proper care.

You’re probably wondering how these metallic marvels would affect your lifestyle. In short, not much would change! Dental implants act like teeth, allowing you to eat, speak, and smile confidently. Taking care of them is the same as taking care of your natural teeth, with regular brushing, flossing, and dentist visits.

Dental implants are quite an investment. However, their permanent nature and superior benefits make them a cost-effective choice in the long run. Several financing options are available to help with the initial expenses, from insurance coverage to payment plans.

qa.q: Who is a candidate for full-mouth dental implants?
qa.a: Adults whose teeth are mostly missing or failing, and people tired of loose dentures. Many already have enough bone; many of the rest qualify after bone grafting or extractions. The cone-beam scan at the consultation answers it for your mouth.

qa.q: How many implants does a full mouth need?
qa.a: Per arch: two or more for a removable implant denture, four for an All-on-4 fixed arch, and up to eight for a fixed bridge on more implants. The scan decides how many your bone will carry.

qa.q: How long does full-mouth treatment take?
qa.a: With All-on-4, about three to four months from surgery to the final zirconia arches, then a further two to four months for complete healing around them. Grafting, if you need it, adds several months of healing before the implants go in.

qa.q: Will I have teeth while the implants heal?
qa.a: Yes. With All-on-4, in most cases you leave the surgery wearing fixed provisional teeth, which stay in place while the implants fuse.

qa.q: How do I look after full-mouth implants?
qa.a: A fixed arch is brushed and flossed like natural teeth and stays in at night. The five-year warranty asks one thing of you: the six-monthly cleanings.

qa.q: Is sedation available for full-mouth surgery?
qa.a: Yes: nitrous oxide or oral sedation, given at the office by the practice's own team. The practice does not offer IV sedation or general anesthesia.

qa.q: Can I really get teeth the same day as my implants?
qa.a: With All-on-4, in most cases yes. You leave the same visit wearing a fixed provisional arch, and the final zirconia arch is fitted three to four months later.

qa.q: Are same-day teeth my final teeth?
qa.a: No. The same-day arch is a provisional in PMMA, fully functional and screwed in place, and it is adjusted at reviews while the implants fuse. The final arch is zirconia.

qa.q: What can I eat with same-day teeth?
qa.a: Soft foods for the next several months, while the implants integrate with the jawbone. That part is not optional, and it is the one people underestimate.

qa.q: Does same-day implant surgery hurt?
qa.a: It is done under local anesthetic with nitrous oxide or oral sedation, so you stay relaxed throughout. Afterwards, patients generally report minor discomfort that over-the-counter medication handles.

qa.q: What if I have bone loss?
qa.a: Bone loss often makes you a candidate for All-on-4 rather than ruling you out, because the rear implants are angled toward denser bone. Some cases still need grafting first, and then the teeth wait for the bone to heal.

qa.q: Can a single tooth be replaced the same day?
qa.a: Sometimes. Where the case allows, the implant goes in at the time of the extraction, and qualifying patients leave with a temporary the same day. The scan shows whether yours qualifies.

sections.h2: Four ways to deal with dentures.

text: Acrylic teeth on a base that rests on the gums. The lowest cost, but they move, need relines and repairs, must come out to clean, and do nothing to stop bone loss.
A removable denture that clips onto two or more implants. It stops slipping, puts load back into the bone and still comes out for cleaning: around 60% of natural function at a moderate cost.
Teeth that never come out: a zirconia bridge screwed onto four to eight implants, often All-on-4 with provisional teeth the same day. Over 98% of natural function, at the highest cost.

sections.h2: What dentures cost, counted over the years.
lead: Traditional dentures cost the least at the start. Over the years the relines, repairs and replacements add up, and the bone keeps receding because nothing loads it.
Snap-in dentures sit in the middle: the implants stop the movement and put load back into the bone, though the denture may still need the occasional reline.

A fixed full arch costs the most up front and the least to keep: no relining, no adhesive, and it is cared for like natural teeth. The figure for your mouth is set at the consultation, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.

qa.q: Why do dentures get loose?
qa.a: Because the jawbone they rest on keeps receding once the teeth are gone, and nothing loads it. A reline refits the denture for a while; anchoring it to implants stops the movement.

qa.q: What are snap-in dentures?
qa.a: Implant-supported dentures: a removable denture that clips onto two or more implants, so it stops slipping but still comes out for cleaning.

qa.q: Can I go from dentures to fixed teeth?
qa.a: Yes. Bone loss from years of wearing a denture often makes you a candidate for All-on-4 rather than ruling you out, and in most cases you leave the surgery wearing fixed provisional teeth. Some mouths need bone grafting first.

qa.q: Who should make my dentures?
qa.a: A prosthodontist: the dental specialist in replacing teeth, dentures included, with three years of training beyond dental school. Dr. Esam Nahlah is a board-certified prosthodontist and sees patients at both offices.

qa.q: What if my denture breaks?
qa.a: Call the office. A broken or damaged denture is treated as an emergency, and space is made to see you the same day wherever possible.

qa.q: Does insurance cover dentures?
qa.a: Most PPO dental plans are accepted, and the practice files the claims for you. What your plan covers is gone through at the consultation, along with the price and the financing.

qa.q: What is full-mouth reconstruction?
qa.a: Rebuilding most or all of the teeth in both jaws to one plan, with crowns, bridges, veneers and implants as the case needs. Prosthodontists call it full-mouth rehabilitation, and it is the core of the specialty.

qa.q: How is it different from a smile makeover?
qa.a: A smile makeover works mostly on the teeth that show. A full-mouth reconstruction rebuilds the whole mouth, back teeth and bite included, often with implants where teeth are missing.

qa.q: Who needs full-mouth reconstruction?
qa.a: Usually people with several problems at once: worn or broken teeth, several missing teeth, gum disease or a bite that no longer meets evenly. The examination and scan decide whether the whole mouth needs rebuilding or only part of it.

lead: A prosthodontist is a dentist who has trained for three more years in replacing and restoring teeth: implants, crowns, bridges, veneers and dentures. Here is how that differs from a general dentist and from a periodontist, and when it matters.

sections.h2: A prosthodontist rebuilds what is missing or broken.
lead: Prosthodontics is one of the dental specialties recognized by the American Dental Association. Its work is rebuilding and replacing teeth: dental implants, crowns, bridges, veneers, complete and partial dentures, and full-mouth rehabilitation. After dental school a prosthodontist trains for three more years in exactly this work, including the laboratory side of making it.
Board-certified Diplomate since 2013
More than 18,000 Implants placed by Dr. Nahlah
More than 15,000 Full arches rebuilt
From 2003 Years in practice

qa.q: What is the difference between a prosthodontist and a periodontist?
qa.a: A periodontist specializes in the gums and the bone that hold teeth, treating gum disease and often placing implants. A prosthodontist specializes in replacing and restoring the teeth themselves. At this practice the prosthodontist plans and places the implants and makes the teeth on them.

qa.q: Is a prosthodontist better than a general dentist?
qa.a: For everyday care, a general dentist is the right first call. For missing teeth, implants, dentures and full-mouth work, a prosthodontist has three more years of training in exactly that, which is why general dentists refer those cases to one.

qa.q: Do I need a referral to see a prosthodontist?
qa.a: You can book a consultation with Dr. Nahlah directly. Dentists who want to refer a patient can do so through the practice's referral page.

qa.q: What does board-certified mean for a prosthodontist?
qa.a: That the prosthodontist has passed the examinations of the American Board of Prosthodontics and is a Diplomate of the Board. Dr. Nahlah became a Diplomate in 2013.

qa.q: Does a prosthodontist place implants?
qa.a: Many do. Dr. Nahlah plans, places and restores implants himself, so the surgery is planned around the teeth that go on top.

qa.q: Where does Dr. Nahlah see patients?
qa.a: At two offices: Suite 220, 7901 Jones Branch Drive in McLean, near Tysons Corner, and 2855 Duke Street in Alexandria.

sections.h2: Where the implant goes is decided on a screen first.
lead: At the Tysons Corner office every implant starts as a cone-beam scan: the jaw in three dimensions, with bone volume and nerve position measured before surgery rather than discovered during it.
The scan Bone and nerves, in 3D
The guide Printed for your mouth
The tooth Designed in the in-house lab

The scan becomes a printed guide, so the implant lands at the planned angle and depth, with smaller incisions and a shorter recovery. One specialist owns all three steps: Dr. Nahlah plans the implant, places it and makes the tooth that sits on it.

sections.h2: Four visits to a finished implant.

text: Time with Dr. Nahlah, a cone-beam scan and an examination. You leave knowing whether you are a candidate, what it costs and how long it will take.
If a tooth has to come out or bone has to be rebuilt, that happens first; grafting brings several months of healing before the implant.
Often a few hours, through the guide made from your scan, with nitrous oxide or oral sedation. Most people are back to normal activity within a week, eating soft food while the implant fuses.
About four months later, once bone has grown onto the post, the final crown, bridge or arch is attached, matched to your shade and bite.

qa.q: Can I be sedated for implant surgery in McLean?

The bone under the gap keeps a load, so it recedes far less
No adhesive, no slipping, nothing taken out at night
Looked after like a natural tooth: brush, floss, six-month visits
Designed to last decades

qa.q: What do dental implants cost in Alexandria?
qa.a: Your price comes from your own scan: how many teeth, how long they have been missing, the materials, and whether bone or gum needs treatment first. It is laid out at the consultation along with insurance and financing, and claims are filed for you.

qa.q: Which number do I call to book?

qa.q: Is it the same specialist as in McLean?
qa.a: Yes. Dr. Esam Nahlah sees implant patients at both offices, with the same team and a laboratory in each building.

qa.q: Will implant surgery hurt?
qa.a: It is done with sedation, so you stay relaxed and feel no pain during it. Afterwards most people manage with over-the-counter medication and are back to normal within about a week.

qa.q: What if I have lost bone?
qa.a: Many patients qualify after bone grafting or extractions. Grafting is its own procedure, with several months of healing before the implant goes in.

qa.q: How do I care for an implant?
qa.a: Like a natural tooth: brush twice a day, floss once, and keep the six-month cleanings, which also keep the five-year warranty.

qa.q: Will I have teeth when I leave the office?

qa.q: What does All-on-4 cost in Alexandria?
qa.a: Your price is set after the scan, once it is clear whether one or both arches need restoring and whether any grafting comes first. Most PPO plans are accepted with claims filed for you, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.

qa.q: What if I have bone loss?
qa.a: Bone loss is often why All-on-4 is chosen: tilting the rear implants reaches bone that straight ones would miss. Some mouths still need grafting first, and the scan shows which.

qa.q: How long until the final teeth?
qa.a: About three to four months after surgery, and then the gum takes another two to four months to settle around the zirconia arch.
